items.explanation: 71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented 2025-03-14 during the admission for embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (prior stroke/TIA 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. No anticoagulant is current at 2026-09-24: her only active clinic orders (2026-07-10) are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine, and no note documents a contraindication, bleeding event or patient refusal. Her 2025-03-14 ECG shows sinus rhythm with one missed/blocked beat, which does not change the need for anticoagulation in paroxysmal AF.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02. Under the revised memo effective 2026-03-01 an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. A 12-lead ECG was recorded on 2026-03-07 (5 days) and documented in the same-day note as sinus rhythm; measured QTc (Bazett) about 370 ms, so the requirement is complete and no QT item is needed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10, his first order of the drug. The memo effective 2026-03-01 required an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart is 107859369 on 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start, so the requirement was not met within the required time (it would have satisfied the superseded 30-day rule). Escitalopram remains current (order 2026-06-20 to 2027-01-03); that late ECG showed sinus rhythm with QTc about 379 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started on the clinic medication list at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order valid to 2026-12-29); the only earlier exposure was a brief perioperative order in December 2025. Under the memo effective 2026-03-01 an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since the start - the last tracing in the chart is 2025-12-25, before it - so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so the memo effective 2026-03-01 required an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. The RN telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no tracing or report is in the chart. Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15; under the memo effective 2026-03-01 an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been recorded since the start (last tracing 2025-03-09, QTc about 414 ms), but the window is still open as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the follow-up is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 the clinician documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily with a plan to recheck. The memo effective 2026-03-01 requires an INR within 7 days of a clinician or clinic-pharmacist dose change, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

The clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily on 2026-09-10 (home INR 3.4), a dose change made under the anticoagulation protocol. The memo effective 2026-03-01 requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since the change - the most recent laboratory INR in the chart is 2.6 on 2026-08-22, and the home INR 3.4 is the result that prompted the change rather than a follow-up - so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old woman who is also on amiodarone.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded 2025-08-22 and carried in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note (2025-10-10 through 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease 1 - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery with prior bypass/graft), so anticoagulation is recommended. No anticoagulant has ever been ordered in clinic; the only current order is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. The remote procedure-related haemorrhage coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter is not documented anywhere as a reason anticoagulation was withheld, so the omission needs prescriber review.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 2026-08-20 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nevertheless re-ordered (current through 2026-12-28) alongside aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, with the note simply stating 'continue current regimen' and no documented review of the bleed or of triple therapy. Apixaban should not continue without prescriber review.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current as of 2026-09-24: rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-25) and apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-26). The 2026-07-15 clinic note states the anticoagulant was being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped and both drugs are listed as current medications in that note. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in this patient with CLL and paroxysmal AF and needs immediate reconciliation.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 348-648 ms) at about 136-142 bpm with no organised P waves - atrial fibrillation, not sinus rhythm at 72 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded for that 2026-06-10 encounter. The documented rhythm conflicts with the same-day tracings and needs correction/review.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily continuously since 2022 (current order 2026-08-22, valid to 2027-01-10), a QT watch-list drug. Her most recent ECG (2022-04-27, the only one after amiodarone was started) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT about 545 ms and RR 1044 ms, giving QTc (Bazett) about 530 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14) potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL are within range; she also takes warfarin and metoprolol. No ECG has been repeated in over four years.

79-year-old man with AF on amiodarone 200 mg daily, started at the 2025-11-10 cardiology clinic visit and still current (order 2026-07-29, valid to 2027-01-05). His most recent ECG (2025-11-24, obtained for the post-start requirement) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT about 520 ms at RR 968 ms, i.e. QTc (Bazett) about 528 ms, above the 500 ms QT-monitoring threshold, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes (2026-04-20) potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL are normal; he remains on warfarin and aspirin as well.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) continuously since 2023-10-02; current order 2026-05-29, valid to 2026-12-25. Her most recent ECG (2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 500 ms at RR 856 ms, i.e. QTc (Bazett) about 540 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required (40 mg is also above the recommended maximum citalopram dose for QT safety). Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01); also on levothyroxine, aspirin and atorvastatin. No repeat ECG since 2023.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10; the memo in force at that time (2025-09-01) required an ECG within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. A 12-lead ECG was obtained on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (The QTc on that ECG is about 528 ms, which is raised separately as a QT safety item.)

No anticoagulant is current at 2026-09-24: her only active clinic orders (2026-07-10) are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine, and no note documents a contraindication, bleeding event or patient refusal. Her 2025-03-14 ECG shows sinus rhythm with one missed/blocked beat, which does not change the need for anticoagulation in paroxysmal AF.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02. Under the revised memo effective 2026-03-01 an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. A 12-lead ECG was recorded on 2026-03-07 (5 days) and documented in the same-day note as sinus rhythm; measured QTc (Bazett) about 370 ms, so the requirement is complete and no QT item is needed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10, his first order of the drug. The memo effective 2026-03-01 required an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart is 107859369 on 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start, so the requirement was not met within the required time (it would have satisfied the superseded 30-day rule). Escitalopram remains current (order 2026-06-20 to 2027-01-03); that late ECG showed sinus rhythm with QTc about 379 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started on the clinic medication list at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order valid to 2026-12-29); the only earlier exposure was a brief perioperative order in December 2025. Under the memo effective 2026-03-01 an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since the start - the last tracing in the chart is 2025-12-25, before it - so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so the memo effective 2026-03-01 required an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. The RN telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no tracing or report is in the chart. Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15; under the memo effective 2026-03-01 an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been recorded since the start (last tracing 2025-03-09, QTc about 414 ms), but the window is still open as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the follow-up is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 the clinician documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily with a plan to recheck. The memo effective 2026-03-01 requires an INR within 7 days of a clinician or clinic-pharmacist dose change, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

The clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily on 2026-09-10 (home INR 3.4), a dose change made under the anticoagulation protocol. The memo effective 2026-03-01 requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since the change - the most recent laboratory INR in the chart is 2.6 on 2026-08-22, and the home INR 3.4 is the result that prompted the change rather than a follow-up - so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old woman who is also on amiodarone.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded 2025-08-22 and carried in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note (2025-10-10 through 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease 1 - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery with prior bypass/graft), so anticoagulation is recommended. No anticoagulant has ever been ordered in clinic; the only current order is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. The remote procedure-related haemorrhage coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter is not documented anywhere as a reason anticoagulation was withheld, so the omission needs prescriber review.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 2026-08-20 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nevertheless re-ordered (current through 2026-12-28) alongside aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, with the note simply stating 'continue current regimen' and no documented review of the bleed or of triple therapy. Apixaban should not continue without prescriber review.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current as of 2026-09-24: rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-25) and apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-26). The 2026-07-15 clinic note states the anticoagulant was being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped and both drugs are listed as current medications in that note. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in this patient with CLL and paroxysmal AF and needs immediate reconciliation.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 348-648 ms) at about 136-142 bpm with no organised P waves - atrial fibrillation, not sinus rhythm at 72 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded for that 2026-06-10 encounter. The documented rhythm conflicts with the same-day tracings and needs correction/review.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily continuously since 2022 (current order 2026-08-22, valid to 2027-01-10), a QT watch-list drug. Her most recent ECG (2022-04-27, the only one after amiodarone was started) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT about 545 ms and RR 1044 ms, giving QTc (Bazett) about 530 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14) potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL are within range; she also takes warfarin and metoprolol. No ECG has been repeated in over four years.

79-year-old man with AF on amiodarone 200 mg daily, started at the 2025-11-10 cardiology clinic visit and still current (order 2026-07-29, valid to 2027-01-05). His most recent ECG (2025-11-24, obtained for the post-start requirement) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT about 520 ms at RR 968 ms, i.e. QTc (Bazett) about 528 ms, above the 500 ms QT-monitoring threshold, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes (2026-04-20) potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL are normal; he remains on warfarin and aspirin as well.

items.explanation: 71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented 2025-03-14 during the admission for embolic cerebral infarction. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (prior stroke/TIA 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. No anticoagulant is current at 2026-09-24: her only active clinic orders (2026-07-10) are carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine, and no note documents a contraindication, bleeding event or patient refusal. Her 2025-03-14 ECG shows sinus rhythm with one missed/blocked beat, which does not change the need for anticoagulation in paroxysmal AF.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02. Under the revised memo effective 2026-03-01 an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. A 12-lead ECG was recorded on 2026-03-07 (5 days) and documented in the same-day note as sinus rhythm; measured QTc (Bazett) about 370 ms, so the requirement is complete and no QT item is needed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10, his first order of the drug. The memo effective 2026-03-01 required an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart is 107859369 on 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start, so the requirement was not met within the required time (it would have satisfied the superseded 30-day rule). Escitalopram remains current (order 2026-06-20 to 2027-01-03); that late ECG showed sinus rhythm with QTc about 379 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started on the clinic medication list at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order valid to 2026-12-29); the only earlier exposure was a brief perioperative order in December 2025. Under the memo effective 2026-03-01 an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since the start - the last tracing in the chart is 2025-12-25, before it - so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so the memo effective 2026-03-01 required an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15; under the memo effective 2026-03-01 an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been recorded since the start (last tracing 2025-03-09, QTc about 414 ms), but the window is still open as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the follow-up is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 the clinician documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily with a plan to recheck. The memo effective 2026-03-01 requires an INR within 7 days of a clinician or clinic-pharmacist dose change, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

The clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily on 2026-09-10 (home INR 3.4), a dose change made under the anticoagulation protocol. The memo effective 2026-03-01 requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since the change - the most recent laboratory INR in the chart is 2.6 on 2026-08-22, and the home INR 3.4 is the result that prompted the change rather than a follow-up - so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old woman who is also on amiodarone.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded 2025-08-22 and carried in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note (2025-10-10 through 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease 1 - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery with prior bypass/graft), so anticoagulation is recommended. No anticoagulant has ever been ordered in clinic; the only current order is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. The remote procedure-related haemorrhage coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter is not documented anywhere as a reason anticoagulation was withheld, so the omission needs prescriber review.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 2026-08-20 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nevertheless re-ordered (current through 2026-12-28) alongside aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, with the note simply stating 'continue current regimen' and no documented review of the bleed or of triple therapy. Apixaban should not continue without prescriber review.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current as of 2026-09-24: rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-25) and apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-26). The 2026-07-15 clinic note states the anticoagulant was being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped and both drugs are listed as current medications in that note. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk in this patient with CLL and paroxysmal AF and needs immediate reconciliation.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 348-648 ms) at about 136-142 bpm with no organised P waves - atrial fibrillation, not sinus rhythm at 72 bpm. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded for that 2026-06-10 encounter. The documented rhythm conflicts with the same-day tracings and needs correction/review.
